title: Lift Up Your Heads, O Gates: The King of Glory
summary: The psalm opens by declaring that the earth and everyone in it belong to the LORD, who founded the world on the seas. It asks who may climb the LORD's hill and stand in his holy place, and answers: those with clean hands and a pure heart. It closes with a processional call to the ancient gates to lift their heads so that the King of Glory, the LORD mighty in battle, the LORD of Hosts, may enter.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 24
from.text: many scholars read it as a processional liturgy with alternating voices

line: The earth is the LORD's; who may climb his hill? Those with clean hands and a pure heart. Then the ancient gates are told to lift their heads for the King of glory.
guide: Hold what you have loosely, since it belongs to God first. Ask what you lift your soul to. Pray verses 7 to 10 aloud with others, as it was first sung: one voice calling, another asking, everyone answering.

stanzas.title: Who may ascend the hill of the LORD?
Lift up your heads: the LORD mighty in battle
Lift up your heads: the LORD of Hosts is the King of Glory

verses.t: A Psalm of David. The earth is the LORD’s, and the fullness thereof, the world and all who dwell therein.
For He has founded it upon the seas and established it upon the waters.
Who may ascend the hill of the LORD? Who may stand in His holy place?
He who has clean hands and a pure heart, who does not lift up his soul to an idol or swear deceitfully.
He will receive blessing from the LORD and vindication from the God of his salvation.
Such is the generation of those who seek Him, who seek Your face, O God of Jacob. Selah
Lift up your heads, O gates! Be lifted up, O ancient doors, that the King of Glory may enter!
Who is this King of Glory? The LORD strong and mighty, the LORD mighty in battle.
Lift up your heads, O gates! Be lifted up, O ancient doors, that the King of Glory may enter!
Who is He, this King of Glory? The LORD of Hosts— He is the King of Glory. Selah
